title: M7.5 Earthquake · Caraballeda, La Guaira, Venezuela
subtitle: Real streets and damage grading · simulated response, teams and indications

response.text: Unit MIA-1 · airlifted 2,200 km · drones up on landing

steps.title: Ready
steps.head: Stations and pilots are in place before the event.
steps.text: Vehicle-mounted drone units and remote-pilot C2 centers are pre-positioned so any disaster zone is reached within 60 minutes.

steps.title: Event occurs
steps.head: M7.5 earthquake strikes La Guaira, Venezuela.
steps.text: Twin shocks, M7.2 and M7.5, 39 seconds apart. Unit MIA-1 is airlifted from Miami; T+ from here counts minutes from its arrival on site.

steps.title: Establish event
steps.head: The unit opens a new Event for central Caraballeda, fully offline.
steps.text: No network needed. The event, its boundary and its team exist on the device from the first minutes.

steps.title: Preload data
steps.head: Layers 1 and 2: the site as it was.
steps.text: Pre-disaster imagery, OpenStreetMap streets and footprints, and building plans were loaded before departure.

steps.title: Capture baseline
steps.head: Layer 3: the site as it is now.
steps.text: The drone's first pass sets the baseline. Compared against Layer 1, it shows what collapsed. Damage here follows the Copernicus EMS grading.

steps.title: Connect & refresh
steps.head: Starlink connects and the picture goes live.
steps.text: Aerial imagery keeps refreshing, and every sensor indication lands on the shared map with its source, time and strength.

steps.title: Teams join
steps.head: Accredited teams join one shared picture.
steps.text: Each team adds data inside its own area, the coordinator resolves conflicts, and the digital twin shows where to dig.
